newsitem.title: USA: Integrated Process expects Q1 loss.
newsitem.headline: Integrated Process expects Q1 loss.

text.p: Integrated Process Equipment Corp said Thursday it expects to post a loss of $0.19 to $0.24 per share in the first quarter ended September 30.

It said the anticipated loss per share widended materially due to lower sales, the absorption of higher overhead on lower sales, the accounting treatment of warrants, continued investment in the next generation of chemical-mechanical planarization and metrology development, and product mix.

Tom McKee, the president and chief operating officer, said in a statement that it was a difficult period for the company because non-chemical-mechanical planarization customers were "continuing to hold back on orders."
"However, intense efforts are expected to produce sequential growth in all product areas for the upcoming quarter," he added.

The company said revenues dropped even further than anticipated during the period, largely based on orders at two subsidiaries - IPEC Clean and IPEC Precision, which are not involved in the chemical-mechanical planarization field.
Integrated Process said it expects to post first-quarter revenues of about $31.8 million. In the 1995 first quarter, the company reported revenues of $38 million.

A third subsidiary, IPEC Planar, has seen an acceleration of orders from an unidentified customer. During the quarter, the customer entered into a binding letter of intent allowing for an acceleration of certain deliveries in the first, second and third quarters of 1997, the company said.
In connection with the letter of intent and rescheduling of shipments, the customer received Integrated Process warrants.
The rescheduled orders accounted for about 20 percent of the first-quarter revenues, the company said.
Integrated Process designs, manufactures, markets and services semiconductor processing equipment.
